questions.question: Vineet, Rajesh and Kriti have different amount of money with them, Rajesh has just double the amount of money than Vineet. The total amount of money that Rajesh and Kriti have is Rs. 147. Kriti has Rs. 6 more than the amount Vineet has. How much money does Kriti have?
questions.questionHtml:
Vineet, Rajesh and Kriti have different amount of money with them, Rajesh has just double the amount of money than Vineet. The total amount of money that Rajesh and Kriti have is Rs. 147. Kriti has Rs. 6 more than the amount Vineet has.

How much money does Kriti have?
questions.solution:
Suppose Vineet has Rs. x.

Rajesh has Rs. 2x.

Kriti has Rs. x + 6.

(2x) + (x + 6) = 147

3x + 6 = 147

3x = 141

x = 47

Vineet has Rs. 47.

Kriti has 47 + 6 = Rs. 53

Hence, 53 is the correct answer.

questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:

Conclusions:

I. Some copies are papers → True (Some papers are copies)

II. Some papers are erasers. → False (it is possible but not definite)

Thus, II and III form a complementary pair.

Therefore, only conclusion I and either conclusion II or III follows.

questions.question: Depreciation is an annual allowance for the wear and tear of ______.
questions.questionHtml: Depreciation is an annual allowance for the wear and tear of ______.
questions.solution:
• Depreciation is an annual allowance for wear and tear of a capital good. In other words, it is the cost of the good divided by a number of years of its useful life.
  • While calculating depreciation unexpected or sudden destruction or disuse of capital as can happen with accidents, natural calamities or other such extraneous circumstances are not taken into account.
  • As an accounting term, depreciation is an expired cost or expense, charged against the revenue of a given accounting period.
  • It is the diminution in the intrinsic value of the asset due to use and/or lapse of time.

questions.question: The total number of images formed by two mirrors inclined at 120° asymmetrically to each other is ______.
questions.questionHtml: The total number of images formed by two mirrors inclined at 120° asymmetrically to each other is ______.
questions.solution:
CONCEPT:

Plane Mirror:

  • A plane mirror is a mirror with a flat (planar) reflective surface.

The number of images formed when the object is placed between two plane mirrors:

⇒ θ = Angle between the two plane mirrors, and n = number of images formed

  • If \(\frac{360}{θ}\) = even number

\(⇒ n=\frac{360}{θ}-1\)

  • If \(\frac{360}{θ}\) = odd number and the object lies symmetrically 

\(⇒ n=\frac{360}{θ}-1\)

  • If \(\frac{360}{θ}\) = odd number and the object lies asymmetrically

\(⇒ n=\frac{360}{θ}\)

  • If \(\frac{360}{θ}\) = fraction 

⇒ n = only integer part of \(\frac{360}{θ}\)

CALCULATION:

Given that: θ = 120° 

Number of images (n) = (360/120) = 3

questions.question: Reema sold 48 articles for Rs. 2,160 and suffered a loss of 10%. How many articles should she sell for Rs. 2,016 to earn a profit of 12%?
questions.questionHtml: Reema sold 48 articles for Rs. 2,160 and suffered a loss of 10%. How many articles should she sell for Rs. 2,016 to earn a profit of 12%?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the formula: (Price1 ÷ (Articles1 × (100 − Loss%))) = (Price2 ÷ (Articles2 × (100 + Profit%)))

2,160 ÷ (48 × 90) = 2,016 ÷ (n × 112)

2,160 ÷ 4,320 = 2,016 ÷ (n × 112)

1 ÷ 2 = 2,016 ÷ (n × 112)

n × 112 = 4,032 ⇒ n = 4,032 ÷ 112 = 36

∴ The correct answer is 36 articles.

Alternate Method

Given: Selling Price (SP1) = Rs. 2,160 for 48 articles, Loss = 10%. Target Profit = 12% for SP2 = Rs. 2,016.

Formulas: CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%) | SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

⇒ SP of 1 article = 2,160 ÷ 48 = Rs. 45

⇒ CP of 1 article = 45 × (100 ÷ 90) = Rs. 50

⇒ Required SP of 1 article for 12% profit = 50 × (112 ÷ 100) = Rs. 56

⇒ Number of articles for Rs. 2,016 = 2,016 ÷ 56 = 36

∴ The correct answer is 36 articles.

Additional Information

Unitary Method in P&L

When solving for multiple articles, it is often easiest to find the Cost Price (CP) of a single unit first.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise in the question.

Add equation (1) and equation (2)

9 (a + b) = 112.5/60

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral in which sides AD and BC are produced to meet at P, and sides DC and AB meet at Q when produced. If ∠A = 60° and ∠ABC = 72°, then ∠DPC –∠BQC = ?
questions.questionHtml: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral in which sides AD and BC are produced to meet at P, and sides DC and AB meet at Q when produced. If ∠A = 60° and ∠ABC = 72°, then ∠DPC –∠BQC = ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary: ∠D = 180° − ∠B = 180° − 72° = 108°.

The angle at the intersection of produced sides is given by ∠P = 180° − (∠A + ∠B) and ∠Q = 180° − (∠A + ∠D).

The difference ∠P − ∠Q = (180° − ∠A − ∠B) − (180° − ∠A − ∠D) = ∠D − ∠B.

∴ ∠DPC − ∠BQC = 108° − 72° = 36°.

∴ The correct answer is 36°.

Alternate Method

Given: ∠A = 60°, ∠ABC = 72° in cyclic quadrilateral ABCD.

Formula Used: Sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°; Sum of angles in a triangle is 180°.

⇒ In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠ADC = 180° − ∠ABC

⇒ ∠ADC = 180° − 72° = 108°

⇒ In ΔPAB, ∠DPC = 180° − (∠A + ∠ABC)

⇒ ∠DPC = 180° − (60° + 72°) = 180° − 132° = 48°

⇒ In ΔQAD, ∠BQC = 180° − (∠A + ∠ADC)

⇒ ∠BQC = 180° − (60° + 108°) = 180° − 168° = 12°

⇒ ∠DPC − ∠BQC = 48° − 12° = 36°

∴ The correct answer is 36°.

Additional Information

Cyclic Quadrilateral Properties

The sum of opposite angles is always 180°. If one side is produced, the exterior angle formed is equal to the interior opposite angle.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles in any triangle is 180°. This property is used to find the angles at the intersection points P and Q.

General Formula

For a cyclic quadrilateral where sides meet at P and Q, the difference between the angles at P and Q is equal to the difference between the opposite interior angles.

questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

A. Although I had a fear of water, I thought it was an important skill I should learn.

B. However, what I didn't realize was that it would also make me a more confident person.

C. I also thought it would be a good exercise that would make me physically stronger.

D. One of the hardest things I've had to do was to learn how to swim.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is DACB.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble. 
  • The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
  • Part D will be the first sentence because it is an independent statement. It mentions about 'one of the hardest things of a person's life'.
  • Part A will be the next in sequence. It has 'although'. You use although to introduce a subordinate clause that contains a statement that contrasts with the statement in the main clause. It mentions the reason behind the speaker learning how to swim despite having fear of water.
  • Part C will be the next in sequence. It has 'also' and states another reason behind learning how to swim.
  • Part B will be the next in sequence. It has 'However'. You use however when you are adding a comment which is surprising or which contrasts with what has just been said. It mentions that the speaker later realized that it helped in increasing confidence.


Thus, the sentences will be arranged as: One of the hardest things I've had to do was to learn how to swim. Although I had a fear of water, I thought it was an important skill I should learn. I also thought it would be a good exercise that would make me physically stronger. However, what I didn't realize was that it would also make me a more confident person.
